title: Unbounded coefficient forgetting identifies canonical etale exchange
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Use the unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For each corner $T$ let $U_T:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ be termwise forgetting of the constant-ring module structure [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. This functor is exact and conservative (it reflects isomorphisms), with $\mathcal H^i(U_TK)=U_T\mathcal H^i(K)$. For every edge $u:A\to B$ there are canonical natural isomorphisms $a_u:U_Au^{-1}_{\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_B$ and $b_u:U_BRu_{*,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{*,\mathbf Z}U_A$. Here $a_u$ is the termwise inverse-image comparison on underlying abelian sheaves, and $b_u$ is the canonical comparison obtained by choosing a module K-injective representative $I$ and an abelian K-injective replacement $U_AI\to J$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], then taking the class of $u_*U_AI\to u_*J$. No preservation of K-injectivity by $U_A$ is asserted.
For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ define the endpoint isomorphisms by the typed composites
$$s_K:U_{Y'}g^{-1}_{\Lambda}Rf_{*,\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{a_g(Rf_{*,\Lambda}K)}g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_YRf_{*,\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}b_f(K)}g^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}Rf_{*,\mathbf Z}U_XK,$$
$$t_K:U_{Y'}Rf'_{*,\Lambda}g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{b_{f'}(g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K)}Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}U_{X'}g'^{-1}_{\Lambda}K\xrightarrow{Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}a_{g'}(K)}Rf'_{*,\mathbf Z}g'^{-1}_{\mathbf Z}U_XK.$$
Thus $s_K$ and $t_K$ identify the forgotten source and target of the exchange with their abelian versions. For the canonical unbounded adjunction-mate exchange maps of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], using the same definition at $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ for abelian sheaves, one has
$$t_K\circ U_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{\square,K})=\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathbf Z}_{\square,U_XK}\circ s_K.$$
No properness, torsion, boundedness, finiteness of $\Lambda$, or isomorphism assertion for either exchange map is assumed or concluded.
